messages:
lucy (Support): New customer Aperture Labs — they completed console flow but there is no usable API key in their production project. Console shows a 'seed_credential' record but the project column is blank. Customer gets 403 calling our API.

lucy (Support): Example from their curl (redacted):
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Key sk-REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"key_not_bound","message":"credential not bound to project"}
```

lucy (Support): claim id they shared: claim/aperture-123. org id: aperture-labs. Can infra folks check provisioning? :eyes:

dmitri (OnboardEng): On it. Most likely a provisioning bootstrap skipped the final bind step (seen this when the template defaults to sandbox). Pushing to check provisioner logs now.

dmitri (OnboardEng): Running: `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/provisioner | grep aperture-123 -n` to see accept/bind sequence 

provision-bot: provisioner: claim aperture-123 accepted at 2026-03-17T14:45:02Z, created credential kc_abc123, attempted bind -> target project 'aperture-staging' (template), expected 'aperture-prod', bind deferred by policy mismatch.

shawn (SRE): That explains the 403 — their app is pointing at prod but the credential is in staging. Two options: rebind kc_abc123 to the prod project, or generate a fresh credential bound to prod and revoke the staging one. Which do you prefer for minimal customer impact?

lucy (Support): Customer wants minimal churn. If we can rebind without rotation that'd be ideal. Are there side effects?

dmitri (OnboardEng): We can reassign metadata in control-plane if the credential hasn't been used for other orgs. Doing a force rebind now: `rwictl provision rebind --claim aperture-123 --cred kc_abc123 --project aperture-prod --force`

dmitri (OnboardEng): Ran rebind at 1768612389, control-plane responded OK. Verifying key visibility for project: `GET /v1/projects/aperture-prod/keys`

provision-bot: control-plane: credential kc_abc123 now bound to project aperture-prod. Audit id audit-77f2. Previous binding to aperture-staging removed.

lucy (Support): Customer retried with same token -> now 401 Unauthorized. They say the token value they used was sk-OLD; looks like we left them with an old token (rotation happened during initial provisioning). 

dmitri (OnboardEng): Ah — the credential id changed. New active token for kc_abc123 is sk-DEF456 (we rotate during rebind to be safe). I just pushed the new token to the customer's secure channel.

lucy (Support): Customer reports success: generate call returned 200, latency nominal. They confirmed app is now calling prod keys. :tada:

shawn (SRE): I'll add a guard in the provisioner templates to stop sandbox mapping for orgs with org_tag:production in the future — filing PR #8423.

dmitri (OnboardEng): Also adding a post-provision verification check (control-plane binding + token sync) to the workflow so this doesn't slip through.

lucy (Support): Marking support ticket as resolved. Thanks all.

shawn (SRE): Nice coordination. :thumbsup:

provision-bot: incident-note: fix applied, audit-77f2, PR-8423 linked to onboarding infra backlog.
